A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and everything you send goes through it.

Normally, websites see your address and your internet provider can see where you go. With a VPN, your data is locked before it leaves your phone or PC, travels through the tunnel, and is unlocked at the VPN company's computer. That computer then talks to the website for you.

So the website sees the VPN's address, not yours, and your provider or anyone on public Wi-Fi sees only scrambled data. The VPN company itself can still see your activity, so pick one you trust.
